analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, 41.0% of finance and insurance firms, NAICS 52, reported using AI in the last two weeks, up from 36.5% in the prior period. The question was first asked in September 2023. This figure covers the broader finance and insurance sector rather than banking alone.

The sector's long-standing AI uses are fraud detection and credit models, which have been in place for decades. Generative AI in customer service and compliance is the newer frontier. The Evident AI Banking Index benchmarks deployment across financial services and scores major global banks on talent, innovation, leadership, and transparency.

Per Evident, several of the world's biggest banks have quietly become AI-powered behemoths, and banks are racing to incorporate the technology into almost everything they do. The index is the closest thing banking has to a public AI scoreboard, but the excerpts do not name specific vendors or report dollar amounts.

The sources do not provide specific ROI figures for banking AI. Evident positions itself as helping leaders make informed decisions and track where technology is starting to unlock value, but no banking ROI numbers appear in the material.

On risk and regulation, Treasury's report on AI in financial services frames uses, opportunities, and risks, per the sourced point. Model risk rules already govern banking AI: credit and AML models operate under Federal Reserve SR 11-7 model risk management guidance issued in 2011, meaning banking AI governance predates the AI boom by more than a decade. A reader deciding whether to deploy should note that adoption is rising and governance expectations are already established, while the available material does not provide ROI evidence to justify investment.

https://evidentinsights.com/.brief: Evident Insights is an intelligence platform that benchmarks and tracks AI adoption across the financial services sector. It supplies data, research, and benchmarking to help financial services leaders make informed AI-related decisions, investments, and strategic choices. The platform publishes the Evident AI Index, which ranks banks and insurers on their AI deployment and highlights emerging trends. Since launching in January 2023, the index has sparked debate and received widespread press coverage, with Evident CEO Alexandra Mousavizadeh frequently commenting on global AI trends.

https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-rel.brief: On International Anti-Corruption Day, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned 28 individuals and businesses tied to a Zimbabwe-based gold smuggling and money-laundering network led by Kamlesh Pattni. The Treasury says the scheme bribed officials, used trusted supporters to conceal ownership, and built a global web of companies to hide illicit activity, depriving Zimbabwe’s citizens of resource benefits while enriching corrupt officials and criminals. Acting Under Secretary Bradley T. Smith noted that “Corruption respects no borders” and that the action demonstrates a whole-of-government approach and collaboration with allies. The Treasury’s move is carried out under Executive Order 13818, which targets serious human-rights abuse and corruption worldwide. International Anti-Corruption Day, observed annually on December 9 since the 2003 UNCAC, aims to raise awareness of anti-corruption initiatives; the United Nations lists 189 parties to the convention.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisi.brief: This page lists the Federal Reserve Board of Governors’ 2011 supervision and regulation letters. It notes that a lock icon or https indicates a secure .gov connection and advises “Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.” It also contains guidance on prior notices concerning dividend declarations by savings association subsidiaries of savings and loan holding companies.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: This page catalogues the 1,000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub, according to the site’s own description. Each entry includes its licence, download count, and release date, and the list is refreshed daily. The data is drawn from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, with every model linking to its own Hub page. The page was last verified on 23 September 2026.
